newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ATHLETICS-RUSSIAN PATIENCE EARNS OLYMPIC GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-RUSSIAN PATIENCE EARNS OLYMPIC GOLD.

text.p: Russian athletics officials will present Marina Shmonina and Lilia Nurutdinova with Olympic gold medals following this weekend's indoor world championships in Paris. The medals are a little late -- five years late, in fact.

The pair ran for the ex-Soviet Unified Team that won the women's 4x400 metres relay in Barcelona in 1992. But they have only just won a marathon appeal to persuade the authorities in Russia and internationally to hand over their medals.

Both women ran in the semifinal but were replaced for the final and were barred from the winners' rostrum, receiving no medal. Olympic rules state, however, that all athletes racing at any stage of the relay competition are entitled to one.
After spending years winning that argument, the two women faced a new hurdle -- the moulds for the Barcelona medals had long since been destroyed for security reasons.
The intervention of Olympic chief Juan Antonio Samaranch saved the day. He ordered copies to be made from specimen medals kept at the International Olympic Committee's museum in Lausanne.
